claims.text: The initial Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a solidified, homogeneous solid solution.
The dynamic mechanical performance of Co-free FeNiCrMn is controlled by temperature- and strain-rate-dependent formation and dissolution of short-range chemical-order clusters.
Short-range chemical-order clusters pin dislocations in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Short-range chemical order modulates a transition from dislocation glide to dynamic strain aging.
Controlled annealing homogenizes the alloy microstructure and removes residual stresses.
At moderate temperatures and strain rates, chemically ordered clusters become more stable.
Stabilized chemically ordered clusters promote dynamic strain aging through dislocation pinning.
Cluster-mediated dislocation pinning enhances work hardening at moderate temperatures and strain rates.
At higher temperatures, the chemically ordered clusters dissolve or become unstable.
At higher strain rates, the chemically ordered clusters dissolve or become unstable.
Cluster dissolution or instability allows dislocation glide to dominate.
Glide dominance following cluster instability results in lower work hardening.
Relative to a baseline alloy without pronounced short-range-order effects, Co-free FeNiCrMn will show increased work hardening at moderate temperatures and strain rates.
Relative to that baseline, Co-free FeNiCrMn will show increased ductility at moderate temperatures and strain rates.
The equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy is an example of a baseline in which dislocation glide predominates without significant short-range-order pinning.
The proposed effect operates only where diffusion is sufficiently active to form or dissolve short-range chemical order.
Very low temperatures or very high strain rates may activate deformation mechanisms outside the proposed short-range-order mechanism.
